Ultraviolette Unveils X-47 Venom: A Shift Toward the Modular VX 100 Platform

The Introduction of the VX 100 Platform

Electric motorcycle manufacturer Ultraviolette has officially launched the X-47 Venom, marking the first vehicle built upon its new VX 100 architecture. Designed to serve as the foundation for future models, this platform prioritizes weight reduction and increased energy efficiency. The move signifies a strategic pivot for the company, focusing on shared engineering principles to streamline development while offering modular battery configurations for consumers.

Battery Specifications and Range

The X-47 Venom is available in two distinct battery configurations. The entry-level model is equipped with a 7.5 kWh battery, offering a claimed range of 227 km. For riders prioritizing long-distance utility, a larger 11 kWh battery variant is available, which provides an extended range of 343 km.

Ultraviolette notes that the move to the VX 100 platform has resulted in tangible physical improvements. The 7.5 kWh version is 17 kg lighter than previous equivalents, while the 11 kWh model also sees weight savings despite its higher capacity compared to the brand's previous 10.3 kWh systems. These changes are complemented by updates to motor efficiency and thermal management systems, though the company indicates that overall top speed and raw performance metrics remain largely consistent with their existing lineup.

Feature Set and Pricing

The pricing for the new motorcycle starts at Rs 2.65 lakh. The flagship variant, featuring the 11 kWh battery pack and the signature 'Afterburner Yellow' aesthetic, is priced at Rs 4.12 lakh.

To differentiate the higher-tier models, Ultraviolette has introduced several convenience-focused technologies. Top-tier variants now include cruise control, a refined TFT instrument cluster, and a dedicated camera system designed to assist with parking maneuvers. Aesthetic options across the range include Stellar White, Turbo Red, Afterburner Yellow, and Cosmic Black.

Considerations for Buyers

While the platform offers notable gains in range and weight management, prospective buyers should note that the engineering refinements—specifically the increased battery density—have resulted in longer charging durations compared to the company’s previous models. As this bike enters a competitive market, it faces pressure from both established electric alternatives and internal combustion motorcycles in a similar price bracket.

Readers interested in the technical specifications or availability should consult the official manufacturer details to verify how these updates align with their specific riding requirements.
